q: How do you structure an ML system design answer?
a: Clarify requirements → define business, model and system metrics → estimate scale → high-level design → deep dive on the hardest parts → failures, monitoring and security → trade-offs and an MVP-first plan.

q: What is p95 latency and why not use the average?
a: The time within which 95% of requests finish. Averages hide slow tails; users making many requests will hit the slow ones, so SLOs are set on p95/p99.

q: Estimate peak requests per second for 6,000 users.
a: Daily requests = users × % active × requests per user (6,000 × 40% × 10 = 24,000). Peak hour share (20%) = 4,800/hour ≈ 1.3/s. Concurrency = rate × duration (Little's law): 1.3 × 4 s ≈ 6 in flight.
Items in the system = arrival rate × time each spends in it. 2 requests/s × 5 s each ≈ 10 requests in progress. It sizes worker pools, connection pools and concurrent LLM streams.

q: What's the most common mistake in design interviews?
a: Jumping to tools or models before clarifying who uses the output, how fast it's needed, the scale and the constraints. The requirements decide batch vs real-time and most of the design.
